The pacing of the story feels natural and well-balanced because the "story time" closely mirrors "real-world time" (the time it takes to read it). The narrative unfolds almost entirely through sparse dialogue and brief stage-like directions, capturing a short, tense conversation in a café. The slight compression of time—such as the few minutes it takes for the waiter to bring the coffee, which passes in the span of five short lines of dialogue—is handled seamlessly through environmental cues (ordering the coffee, the coffee arriving, a bus passing by). Meanwhile, the brief moments of silence and physical hesitation (moving the sugar bowl, touching the jacket) slightly stretch the emotional beats without dragging the scene out, effectively building the unspoken tension between the two characters.
